title: Zadar With a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Costs, Verdict
metaDescription: Zadar with a dog in 2027: dog beaches, Old Town and restaurant rules, ferries, park rules, hotel dog fees, summer heat, vets and EU pet passport rules.
content:
## Are dogs allowed on beaches in Zadar?

Only on designated beaches. Croatian rules bar dogs from public swimming beaches in the main swimming season, roughly mid-May to mid-September, unless the beach is signed as a *plaža za pse* or *pasja plaža*. Those are the two phrases to look for on signs and maps.

Options in and around Zadar:

- **Zaton Holiday Resort:** a fenced-off section of the Blue Flag sandy beach is set aside for dogs. It is about 16 km from central Zadar, in the direction of Nin.
- **Foša:** a small swimming spot at the harbour inside the Old Town. It is tiny, but it works for a quick cool-down after a walk through the streets.
- **Punta Bajlo and Sv. Klement:** the Punta Bajlo promenade has quiet rocky entries that dogs use. A dog-friendly zone has been reported at the Sv. Klement islet, separated from the renovated beach. Look for signs on arrival, because designations change between seasons.
- **Dog Beach Bartovica:** a dog-friendly beach in Zadar County with a gradual entry into the water. A car is needed to reach it.
- **Privlaka:** a long sandy bay about 20 km from Zadar, with a dog-friendly section.
- **Sakarun, Dugi Otok:** a white-sand beach popular with dog owners, reached by ferry.

Outside the main swimming season, from late September to April, enforcement on ordinary beaches is relaxed and dogs are commonly walked there on a leash.

**Tip:** Zadar's own dog-beach offer is small. The best sand and space for dogs is 15–20 km outside the city, so book accommodation with parking.

## Dogs in Zadar Old Town and restaurants

The Old Town peninsula is flat, car-free and paved with polished limestone. That suits dogs, but the stone gets very hot in July and August. Check it with the back of your hand and walk the Riva at dawn or after 19:00. Dogs must be leashed at all times. Muzzles are legally required only for breeds listed as dangerous, but carry one anyway for ferries.

Most restaurants and cafés allow dogs on outdoor terraces. Indoor dining is usually refused, in line with food-hygiene rules. Ask before sitting. Shaded parks work well in the afternoon, and Zadar has several dog parks, including Višnjik and one at the former barracks site.

## National parks near Zadar

- **Paklenica** (about 45 minutes to 1 hour from Zadar): leashed dogs are allowed on most trails. It is the best park for energetic dogs, but the canyon floor needs water and a cool start.
- **Krka** (about 1 hour): dogs are allowed on a leash at all times. They are not allowed on Visovac Island, and some sources say they are not allowed on the park boats. Muzzles may be required on park shuttles. Dogs should not swim in the lakes or rivers.
- **Kornati** is reached by excursion boat. Operators set their own pet rules, so ask when booking.

Plitvice also allows leashed dogs, but its crowded boardwalks suit calm dogs only.

## Ferries and catamarans from Zadar

Jadrolinija runs the car ferries and catamarans to Ugljan, Pašman, Dugi Otok and other islands. Rules by vessel type:

- **Car ferries:** dogs travel on the open deck, leashed and muzzled, not in passenger lounges. Several sources list this as free. Others mention a fee, sometimes quoted as about half the passenger fare. Confirm at the ticket window.
- **Catamarans and fast boats:** small dogs up to 8 kg in a carrier (maximum 45 × 35 × 25 cm) are the safe case. Larger dogs have been refused on some catamarans since a veterinary inspection, and other sources report paid deck boxes. Check the specific line before you travel.

The practical rule: take the slower car ferry with a big dog.

## What accommodation charges for a dog

Pet fees in coastal Croatia typically run **€5–15 per night**. Some hotels charge a flat cleaning fee instead. Pet-friendly hotels in Zadar start from about €65 per night for a double. Private apartments are the most common pet-friendly option, and many do not charge at all. Ask about the fee and the size limit before you book. Campsites usually allow dogs but keep them out of pools and off the beach. A typical camp near Zadar sets a 60 kg limit and requires a leash.

## Summer heat and the best months

July and August bring around 30°C air temperature and hot pavement. Dogs are at risk of heatstroke on midday walks and in parked cars. Never leave a dog in a vehicle.

- **Best months:** May, June, September and October. The sea is warm enough for swimming, trails are comfortable, and beaches are less crowded.
- **Good for walks only:** November to April. The weather is mild and the Old Town is quiet.
- **Avoid if possible:** mid-July to mid-August.

A useful rule: plan activity before 10:00 and after 18:00 in summer.

## Vet basics

Zadar is the best-equipped base in northern Dalmatia for veterinary care, with clinics in town and an emergency service. Typical costs if something is needed locally are a microchip at €15–25 and a rabies vaccination at €25–50. Ask your accommodation for the nearest emergency clinic before you need one. In summer the main risks are ticks, sandflies and heat. Use tick and flea protection, and keep fresh water and a collapsible bowl on every walk. Dogs should not drink seawater or stagnant water.

## EU pet passport rules for driving in

- **Microchip:** ISO 11784/11785, implanted before or on the same day as the rabies vaccine. If the chip date comes later, the vaccine is treated as invalid.
- **Rabies vaccination:** valid for the whole trip. Wait at least 21 days after the first vaccination before travelling.
- **Document:** an EU pet passport issued by an authorised vet. Under rules applying from 22 April 2026, passports are issued only to owners whose main home is in an EU state. Travellers from the UK (Great Britain) or other non-EU countries need an animal health certificate instead. Northern Ireland remains in the scheme.
- **Minimum age:** about 105 days for entry.
- **No tapeworm treatment** is required for Croatia.
- **Border checks:** Croatia is in Schengen. Document checks on pets can still happen on entry from a non-Schengen country such as Bosnia or Serbia.

## Verdict: how dog-friendly is Zadar?

**Zadar rates 3.5 out of 5 as a dog-friendly destination.** The city is excellent for walks: flat, compact, with terraces that welcome dogs and several dog parks. It is weaker for swimming, because the city has few dog beaches. You need a car for Zaton, Privlaka or Bartovica. Choose Zadar for a spring or autumn trip with a dog that tolerates leashes and ferries. For a beach-focused August holiday, pick a resort with its own dog beach instead.

faq.question: Is Zadar dog-friendly?
faq.answer: Yes, moderately. Dogs are welcome on a leash in the Old Town, in parks and on most restaurant terraces. Swimming is the weak point, because the city has few designated dog beaches.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on beaches in Zadar in summer?
faq.answer: Only on beaches signed as plaža za pse. Ordinary public beaches ban dogs during the main swimming season, roughly mid-May to mid-September. Zaton Holiday Resort has a dog section about 16 km from the centre.

faq.question: Can dogs take the ferry from Zadar to the islands?
faq.answer: Yes. On Jadrolinija car ferries, dogs stay on the open deck, leashed and muzzled. Catamarans are stricter: small dogs up to 8 kg in a carrier are accepted, while larger dogs may be refused.

faq.question: How much do hotels charge for a dog in Zadar?
faq.answer: Usually €5–15 per night. Some apartments charge nothing, and some hotels add a one-off cleaning fee. Pet-friendly hotels start at about €65 per night.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia?
faq.answer: An ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport. Travellers from the UK (Great Britain) and other non-EU countries use an animal health certificate. The chip must be implanted before the rabies shot.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Zadar with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October. The weather is warm for swimming and walking, and beaches are quieter. July and August bring around 30°C and hot pavement, which is hard on dogs.

quickAnswer: Zadar is moderately dog-friendly. Leashed dogs can walk the flat Old Town and sit on most restaurant terraces. Main city beaches ban dogs in summer, so use designated dog beaches such as the one at Zaton Holiday Resort. Accommodation usually charges €5–15 per night. Visit in May, June or September–October, with a microchip, rabies vaccination and EU pet passport.
